title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Trailing multiples on firms mid-carveout fool quick screens. Real valuation starts with core Enterprise Value versus free cash.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: At the verified 2026-11-12 close, AXISCADES traded at ₹1,918.30 on NSE [1]. At ₹1,918.30 across 4.277 Cr diluted Screener shares, equity cap equals ₹8,204.57 Cr (Screener shows ₹8,220 Cr at ₹1,922) [1, 2]. Automated screens flag a trailing P/E of 251x (Screener) due to Q1 FY27 exit write-offs [2]. We must strip away both accounting noise and deferred deal timing to price the continuing hardware core [3].

Why did Q1 FY27 print a loss? Under Ind AS 105, AXISCADES split out exited Akkodis services and booked ₹21.81 Cr in exit costs [4]. Continuing Q1 sales hit ₹183.4 Cr (₹733.6 Cr annualized) alongside management-defined normalized EBITDA of ₹41.0 Cr, yet net PAT printed -₹14.8 Cr [4, 5]. On clean FY26 net profit (₹72 Cr; EPS ₹16.92), shares trade at 113.4x trailing P/E and 48.3x FY26 EBITDA (₹8,592.57 Cr EV / ₹178 Cr) [6].

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF model tests what ₹1,918.30 already bakes in [7]. Credit only Year-1 expected Akkodis cash (-₹945.93 Cr), and buyers pay ₹7,646.64 Cr EV today for the continuing core [8]. Even assuming debt falls to zero, Cloud Wave + ITSJ + DAL spend ~₹454 Cr cash in Year 1 [8]. With normalized Q1 continuing EBITDA at ₹41 Cr (₹164 Cr annualized), reaching the ₹270 Cr FY27E goal demands massive H2 scaling [9]. Using 12.0% WACC and 65% FCF conversion, justifying ₹7,646.64 Cr requires EBITDA to compound ~24% annually for eight years with zero working-capital drains [9].

web_blocks.caption: Quantitative Head-to-Head Peer Comparison (2026-11-12 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: AXISCADES shows a distorted trailing P/E (Screener 251x, TradingView live pull 226x) because of Q1 FY27 one-time charges. It earns 15.4% ROCE and 11.5% ROE, well below BEL (36.4% ROCE, 45.8x P/E) and Data Patterns (21.9% ROCE, 99.3x P/E). Peer-table prices come from a TradingView pull on 2026-11-13; the prose uses the 2026-11-12 ledger closes.

web_blocks.html: Verified 2026-11-12 peer data underscores the valuation risk [10]. BEL closed at ₹404.80 (Stage 1) with 36.4% ROCE and 27.5% ROE [11]. Data Patterns closed at ₹4,231.00 (Stage 3) with 21.9% ROCE and ~40% margins [12]. Astra Microwave closed at ₹1,785.80 (Stage 3) with 20.3% ROCE [13]. AXISCADES lags on capital returns (15.4% ROCE, 11.5% ROE) and FCF (-₹135 Cr), yet trades at 28.3x Year-1 Core EV/EBITDA [14]. Paying peak multiples when the entire defense group sits in Stage 3 offers zero margin of safety [15].

Sensitivity math confirms weak asymmetry at ₹1,918.30 [8, 9]. Suppose Year-1 cash reaches ₹945.93 Cr, then pays off ₹388 Cr debt, ₹260 Cr Cloud Wave EV, ₹59.5 Cr ITSJ, and ₹134 Cr capex [6, 8]. Only +₹104.4 Cr net cash remains before any unwind of the 220-day payable stretch (~₹161 Cr drain on +60d normalization) [8]. At conservative ₹234 Cr continuing FY28E EBITDA and 22x multiple, stressed fair value drops to ₹1,230/sh (-36%) [9]. Even valuing ₹285 Cr FY28E EBITDA at 26x plus staged cash yields ₹2,030/sh Base Case—just +5.82% upside [9].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Pay Peak Multiple for Uncollected Promises
paragraphs: Peer math and staged cash timing carry a clear warning. Counting 100% of a 30-month divestment on day one flatters valuation, while Year-1 cash barely covers debt, M&A, and plant capex.
If suppliers demand normal 120–140 day terms instead of 220 days, Year-1 cash cushion vanishes. At ₹1,918.30 (Stage 3), risk outweighs reward.

web_blocks.html: Valuation Trigger: Keep fair value conservatively discounted until Q2/Q3 FY27 continuing EBITDA clears ₹65+ Cr quarterly, debtor days drop under 100, and Days Payable normalize below 140 without pulling CFO negative.

book_paragraphs: Valuation is where this dossier is strictest. We separate three things that screens blend together: the accounting noise in trailing earnings, the timing of the Akkodis cash, and the earnings power of the continuing business.
Only after those three are separated can we ask what the share price already assumes.

One more check keeps the valuation honest: compare what the market pays per rupee of EBITDA with what that rupee earns. BEL earns a 36.4% return on capital and Data Patterns earns 21.9%. AXISCADES earns 15.4%. A business with lower returns on capital should not command a higher multiple of EBITDA than peers that convert capital into profit faster, unless its growth is clearly superior and clearly funded.

The growth case is real but unproven. Continuing revenue grew 94% in the first quarter of FY27, and defense revenue more than doubled. The base is small, however, and the quarter included lumpy dispatches. We therefore treat the quarter as encouraging evidence and keep our base case below the level that would require every guided number to arrive on time.

book_subsections.title: Sum-of-the-Parts Reality: Counting Only the Cash That Has Arrived
paragraphs: A sum-of-the-parts bridge starts from the market value of equity and adjusts for debt and for cash that belongs to shareholders. At the ₹1,918.30 close on 4.277 crore diluted shares, equity is ₹8,204.57 crore, or ₹1,918.30 per share. Add ₹388 crore of borrowings, about ₹90.72 per share, and gross enterprise value is ₹8,592.57 crore, or ₹2,009 per share.

Now apply the Akkodis proceeds honestly. The deal is worth about 237 million dollars in headline terms. The 51% initial stake in aerospace services plus the full services unit sale brings roughly 135.8 million dollars in Year 1. After about 17.5% for tax and fees, that is close to ₹946 crore, or ₹221 per share. Subtracting it leaves a Year-1 continuing core enterprise value of ₹7,646.64 crore, or ₹1,788 per share.

The remaining 49% of aerospace services, about ₹704 crore, comes later and depends on escrow and earn-out terms. Even if every rupee of it arrives, the full pro-forma core enterprise value is ₹6,942.57 crore, or 25.7 times guided EBITDA. At no point on this ladder does the stock look cheap against 15.4% ROCE. Peers such as BEL earn 36.4% ROCE and Data Patterns earns 21.9%, and several of them trade at similar or lower multiples of EBITDA.

book_subsections.title: Walkthrough of the Reverse DCF: What Growth Does ₹1,918.30 Demand?
paragraphs: A reverse DCF asks what the market must believe. We use a 12.0% cost of capital, 4.5% terminal growth, and a cash conversion of 65% of EBITDA. That conversion is far better than FY26, when operating cash flow was minus ₹1 crore on ₹178 crore of EBITDA. The assumption is generous on purpose, so that any shortfall belongs to the business and not to our model.

With a Year-1 continuing enterprise value of ₹7,647 crore, EBITDA must compound at roughly 24% a year for eight years. That takes ₹270 crore in FY27 to about ₹1,500 crore by FY35. It must do so without a single working-capital blowout, and with acquisitions at Cloud Wave and ITSJ integrated cleanly. Few Indian defense or engineering names have held that pace for that long.

Management's own first quarter makes the near-term bar higher. Normalised EBITDA of ₹41.0 crore annualises to about ₹164 crore. Reaching ₹270 crore means the next three quarters must average about ₹76 crore each. That is possible if defense dispatches bunch into the second half, as management says. It is not something an investor should pay for in advance.

book_subsections.title: Sensitivity: Bear, Base and Bull Without Wishful Cash
paragraphs: Bear case. Suppose only the Year-1 cash of ₹946 crore arrives. It pays down ₹388 crore of debt, funds ₹260 crore for Cloud Wave, ₹59.5 crore for ITSJ and about ₹134 crore of capex. That leaves about ₹104 crore. Continuing FY28 EBITDA reaches ₹234 crore, and the market pays 22 times. Equity value is ₹5,148 crore plus ₹104 crore, or ₹5,252 crore. On 4.277 crore shares that is about ₹1,230 per share, a fall of 35.9%.

Base case. Phased proceeds of ₹1,650 crore arrive, debt is repaid, and FY28 continuing EBITDA reaches ₹285 crore at 26 times. Enterprise value is ₹7,410 crore. Adding ₹1,650 crore and subtracting ₹388 crore of debt gives ₹8,672 crore, or about ₹2,027 per share. We carry ₹2,030, a gain of 5.8%. Bull case reaches ₹2,650 on ₹325 crore at 30 times.

Weighting 25% bear, 55% base and 20% bull gives ₹1,954, only 1.9% above the close. A 1.9% expected gain over twelve months does not pay for the risk of a 36% drawdown. That arithmetic is the heart of the REJECTED verdict. It does not say the company is bad. It says the price already pays for the good outcome.

book_callouts.title: VALUATION BRIEF: WHAT THE PRICE ALREADY PAYS FOR
book_callouts.quote: Count the cash that is in the bank, not the cash in the press release.
book_callouts.text: At ₹1,918.30 the Year-1 continuing core trades near 28.3 times FY27 guided EBITDA. Weighted twelve-month value is ₹1,954, a +1.9% expected return.
